- When sentiment is positive (≥0.33) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 1–2% relative to model output.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.20), model often underestimates or fails to anticipate sharp drops; increase forecast lows by 1–2% to avoid under-shock.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., 76+), producing exaggerated upward momentum in 30d forecast; cap 30d forecast peaks at 10–15% below prior 18d high.
- Model shows persistent lag in mean reversion: fails to correct downward trends quickly; add 1–2% upward bias in 30d forecast for 3–5 consecutive days of falling prices.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.00) and price is trending, model often misjudges direction; use 3-day moving average of recent 18d to anchor forecast midpoint.
- Avoid forecasting sharp reversals without prior sentiment signal; if sentiment is flat for 3+ days, model should not predict >5% swing in 30d horizon unless confirmed by price action.
